Operational note on wind-down assistance: 30 days of "free" effort often balloons depending on integration complexity. Typical items and rough estimates:
- Data export + verification: ~12–24 engineering hours (depending on dataset size)
- Knowledge transfer sessions with platform ops: 6–10 hours of SMEs (2–3 sessions)
- Customer-specific scripts or support to turn on exports: 8–16 hours

We can offer a 30-day window for data export/read-only access at no charge, but any active migration assistance beyond standard exports should be capped and billed. If Acme wants us to run an import into a new platform or provide dedicated engineer time, we'd need a SOW or billable hours. Also note that any assistance requiring elevated access or special retention of logs needs security review.

Happy to flesh out a short statement of scope and an estimate we can attach to our counter.

Commercially, we should avoid a fixed $100k cap unless paired with strong carve-outs. Counter proposal ideas:

- Cap = greater of (12 months of prepaid fees, $250k) — aligns with deal economics and gives us predictability.
- Carve-outs to include IP infringement, indemnifiable third-party claims, and damages from gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Consequential damages remain excluded, but carve for confidentiality/data breaches (i.e., those damages can be recoverable).
- Termination refund: pro-rated unused prepaid fees for active subscriptions, subject to offset for a one-month minimum (prevents gaming). No refunds for consumed professional services or SOW work.
- Wind-down: provide 30 days of read-only access + standard export at no charge; offer billable migration hours or a separate short SOW cap (e.g., 40 hours at our standard rates).

If legal can draft concise redline language, we can present this as our go-to position. I can present these options on the commercial call and push for the fee-based migration if they insist on deeper assistance.

Team —

Draft legal positions / suggested redline language (high level):

1) Limitation of Liability (LoL):
   - Proposed: The aggregate liability of each party arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the total fees paid or payable by Customer to Provider under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) US$250,000.

2) Carve-outs from LoL:
   - Liability for (a) breach of confidentiality obligations, (b) willful misconduct or gross negligence, and (c) third-party indemnity obligations (including IP infringement) shall not be limited by the LoL.

3) Consequential Damages:
   - Excluded except to the extent such damages are directly resulting from a breach of confidentiality obligations or an indemnifiable third-party claim—these shall be recoverable to the extent permitted by law.

4) Termination / Refunds:
   - If Customer terminates for convenience, Provider will refund prepaid subscription fees for unused full billing periods on a pro-rata basis, less an amount equal to one (1) month of fees. No refunds for professional services or SOW deliverables already performed. If Provider terminates for material breach by Customer, Provider may retain prepaid fees as offset for winding down.

5) Wind-down Assistance:
   - Provider will make available 30 days of read-only access and standard export tools at no additional charge. Any active migration work (engineering, runbook creation, or hands-on transfer) will be made available under a separate SOW or through a capped billable support engagement (examples: up to 40 hours at standard rates).

6) Practical negotiation tips for the call with Acme:
   - If Acme insists on a low fixed cap ($100k), respond with our cap tied to 12 months' fees or $250k and emphasize carve-outs for confidentiality and IP.
   - Keep refund mechanics simple: pro-rata unused subscription fees with one-month minimum; preserve ability to bill for hands-on migration.

If you approve, I'll produce a redline with the exact contract text and track changes to their doc.

-Rishi
Senior Counsel, Contracts

Hi Susan —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We're broadly aligned on the mechanics but have some differences on caps and scope of complimentary wind-down assistance. To close efficiently, here's our proposed compromise for discussion on the call:

1) Limitation of liability: cap at the greater of (i) 12 months of fees paid under the Order Form, or (ii) $250,000. This balances risk for both parties and scales with the economics of the contract.
2) Carve-outs: carve-outs for IP infringement, willful misconduct/gross negligence, and indemnified third-party claims. Confidentiality/data breaches are carve-outs for recovery (i.e., damages arising from those events are not limited by the cap).
3) Consequential damages: generally excluded except where directly arising from a carve-out event as noted above.
4) Termination/refund: pro-rated refund of unused prepaid subscription fees for full billing periods, subject to an offset equal to one month of fees. No refunds for professional services or SOW deliverables (performed work).
4) Wind-down assistance: 30 days of read-only access + standard export tooling at no charge. Any hands-on migration or dedicated engineering time would be scoped and billed (e.g., capped SOW of up to 40 hours) — we can include a line item in the Order Form if Acme wants that included.

Would Acme be available for a brief 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through these positions and resolve the redlines? We aim to produce a tracked-redline version of the MSA with these changes if you agree in principle.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
